title: 01 — Tool-generated producer / creator strings (P6 suppression list)
consumer: the §2.2/§2.3 producer-creator discount rule, tier 1 (Suppression) — a match produces **no fact in any field** and one `unresolved` row with `reason = discounted_tool_metadata`
match_field: `observation.raw_value` where `location.zone == metadata` and the `field`-kind segment's label is one of the property names below
normalization_for_matching: Compare against the raw value with Unicode NFC applied and leading/trailing whitespace stripped, **for comparison only**. P4 RAW-1/RAW-2 keep the stored `raw_value` byte-for-byte untouched; this normalization exists inside P6's matcher and never writes back.
boundary_rule: A `prefix` entry fires when the normalized value **equals** the prefix, or when it begins with the prefix followed by a *boundary character* and a *version tail*. A boundary character is one of ` `, `\t`, `,`, `;`, `:`, `/`, `(`, `)`, `-`, `_`, `.`, `+`, `&`, `®`, `™`, `©` — never a letter or a digit, which is what stops `Notion` matching `Notional` and `iText` matching `iTextbook`. A version tail is a remainder that **contains at least one ASCII digit**, which is what stops `Microsoft Word` matching `Microsoft Word skills certificate`. An entry may set `tail_required: "any"` to drop the digit requirement; only one row does, and it carries its own false-positive analysis. `exact` entries compare the whole normalized value. **Known residual:** a value that both begins with a tool name and contains a digit for another reason (`Microsoft Office 365 invoice`) still matches. This is accepted, not overlooked: such a string is not a realistic Producer/Creator/Author value, and P6's *Demotion* tier bounds the cost of any false positive here to one lost `authored_by`, a field §3.8 already makes `destination_eligible = FALSE`.
design_cites: §2.2: "PDF metadata should be treated as supporting evidence, not as truth. Author and creator fields may be stale, generic, or generated by a tool rather than a person, so a value such as `python-docx`, `Mozilla/5.0`, or a browser-generated producer string should not be mistaken for meaningful content." — the three settled seeds are entries `tps-python-docx`, `tps-ua-mozilla-5`, and the browser class (`tps-ua-*`).
P5 SPEC E1: "They are emitted verbatim (the raw value is never discarded, §2.8) at `zone = metadata` with `reliability: direct` — `direct` describes the **slot**, not the value's usefulness."
P5 SPEC E1 / M4: "There is no marker on the observation. P5 sets no suppression flag and invents no field: the producer/creator discount rule is P6's."
P6 SPEC, *Suppression*: "It is not downgraded to `possible`; a tool name is not a weak clue about the document, it is a fact about the software."

P6 SPEC, *Demotion*: any value NOT on this list "may populate an authorship role field (§3.8 `authored_by`) and nothing else" — so a miss here is a contained recall loss, never a wrong destination (§3.8 makes every authorship field `destination_eligible = FALSE`).

P2 SPEC A4 adversarial case: "generic author metadata (`python-docx`, `Mozilla/5.0`, browser producer strings) | metadata trust | metadata retained as supporting evidence only | a facet, group, or destination dimension keyed on creator identity".

property_names.note: The property names this list is evaluated against. P4 D7 stores "the source format's own slot name, verbatim", so the label is the format's spelling, not a normalized one. A slot not on this list is not a discount target.

rules: **No human author names.** No entry may match a string that is a plausible personal name. This is the rule that keeps a Creator of `Jane Chen` off the list; it is also why bare `Adobe`, bare `Prince`, bare `Canon`, and bare `Nikon` are refused below rather than matched.

**Exact by default.** `prefix` is used only where the tool appends a version and the false-positive analysis is written into the row. `regex` is used only where the tool token sits in the middle or end of the value (`Quartz PDFContext`, browser UA tokens).
**P5 never sees this list.** It is injected into P6 only; nothing here may become a module-level constant inside `src/extractors/` (P5 PLAN Global Constraints / Task 20).
**Suppression, not demotion.** A match writes no fact in any field, including `authored_by`. A near-miss is not downgraded — it takes the ordinary demotion path.
**No dates.** Nothing here parses or matches a date; §3.10 is P6's separate deferred row.
coverage_note: v1 covers the PDF producer/creator engines, Office and Office-compatible writers, browser user-agent strings, and the imaging tools that stamp EXIF/PNG `Software` — the four families §2.2 and §2.6 actually name. It deliberately does **not** enumerate camera firmware strings, scanner-model strings, or per-vendor MFP producer strings: those are open-ended vendor sets whose members change per model, and entry `tps-bare-version` already catches the bare-version-number form most of them take in a `Software` slot. Camera **filename** patterns are catalogue 04, not here. Growth path: add a row when a real corpus surfaces a string, with the same six evidence columns.

injection: P6 receives this list as data at construction — `FactResolver(..., tool_producer_strings=load('01-tool-producer-strings.json'))` or the P1-namespaced configuration object equivalent. It is **not** imported as a module-level constant, and it is never imported anywhere under `src/extractors/`: P5 emits the producer value verbatim with no flag (M4), and Task 20's runtime-introspection guard fails if any producer string appears in an `extractors` module namespace.

entries.rationale: Figma stamps its name into exported PDF metadata.
entries.design_cite: §2.2, §2.9 design/creative

entries.rationale: Sketch writes `Sketch.app` — the `.app` suffix is required, because bare `Sketch` is an ordinary noun and is refused.
entries.design_cite: §2.2, §2.9 design/creative

entries.rationale: Notion's PDF export stamps its own name. Boundary rule keeps `Notional` out.
entries.design_cite: §2.2 "generated by a tool rather than a person"

entries.rationale: A metadata value that is nothing but a dotted version number is a software version — phone OS builds land in EXIF `Software` this way (`17.5.1`), as do camera firmware stamps. It is never a person and never a subject, so it must not become an `authored_by`. This single row is why v1 does not need to enumerate per-model camera firmware strings.
entries.design_cite: §2.2 "generated by a tool rather than a person"; §2.6 "software metadata"

entries.rationale: Writer-library placeholders that fill an empty slot. Suppressing them is the same act as suppressing a tool name: the value is an artefact of the writer, not a statement about the document. Anchored whole-value.
entries.design_cite: §2.2 "Author and creator fields may be stale, generic, or generated by a tool rather than a person"

refused.rationale: Named in the task as the worked ambiguity. Refused as a bare token: it is a company name that can legitimately be an organizational author, and the concrete Adobe product strings (`Adobe Acrobat`, `Adobe PDF Library`, `Adobe InDesign`, `Adobe Illustrator`, `Adobe Photoshop`, `Adobe LiveCycle`) already cover every case where the value is a tool. Preferring the known product tokens over the bare vendor name is the choice this list makes wherever a vendor name is ambiguous.
refused.design_cite: §2.2 "generated by a tool rather than a person" — the discriminator is *tool*, and `Adobe` alone does not name one

refused.rationale: A common given name and surname. Only the version-suffixed form (`tps-prince`) matches.
An ordinary English noun and a plausible document subject. Only the `Safari/<digits>` UA token matches.

refused.match: Canon / Nikon / Sony / Epson / HP / Xerox / Brother
refused.rationale: Bare scanner and camera vendor names. They appear in EXIF `Make` — which is not a slot on this list — and in scanner Producer strings whose model tails are an open-ended per-device set. Refused rather than guessed; a real corpus should drive any addition, and `tps-bare-version` already catches the firmware-version form.
refused.design_cite: §2.6 names camera make as its own field, separate from software metadata

refused.rationale: A legitimate organizational author. The product-specific rows cover the tool cases. Listed in `uncertain` so Joseph can decide, not silently matched.

The list's first rule, stated as a refusal so it is testable: a Creator of `Jane Chen` matches nothing here and therefore takes the demotion path — it may fill `authored_by` and nothing else. This is the acceptance case named in the brief.
refused.design_cite: P6 SPEC *Demotion*: "Any other producer/creator/author metadata value … may populate an authorship role field (§3.8 `authored_by`) and nothing else"

uncertain.rationale: Widely reported as the generator string on Google Docs exports, but no vendor or standards source confirming it was found on 2026-08-20. The Google Docs **PDF** export path is already covered with a cited source via `tps-skia-pdf` (`Skia/PDF m…`), so omitting this loses little. Needs one real Google Docs → DOCX/ODT export inspected before it is promoted.

wkhtmltopdf's Qt backend reportedly writes `Qt 4.8.7` into Producer. Only blog-tier sourcing found. A whole-value regex `^Qt \d+\.\d+(\.\d+)?$` would be safe, but the string also appears from other Qt applications, and `tps-wkhtmltopdf` already catches the common case.

Should a bare `Microsoft` / `Microsoft Corporation` in an Author slot be suppressed, or demoted to `authored_by = Microsoft`? Suppression loses a true organizational authorship fact; demotion admits a value that is usually a template artefact. Currently refused (demoted). Joseph's call.
uncertain.design_cite: §2.3 "may identify a prior editor, a document template, or a script"

uncertain.match: User / Admin / Administrator / Owner / Guest / student
uncertain.rationale: OS account defaults that land in `lastModifiedBy` and `Author`. They are not tool *names*, so they sit outside §2.2's literal wording, but they are exactly as uninformative and §2.3's "a prior editor" reasoning covers them. Suppressing them is defensible; it is a policy step past the design's text, so it is deferred to Joseph rather than taken here.
uncertain.design_cite: §2.3 "may identify a prior editor, a document template, or a script rather than the meaningful subject or purpose"

uncertain.match: Canon iR-ADV / KONICA MINOLTA bizhub / RICOH MP / Xerox WorkCentre / HP Digital Sending Device
uncertain.rationale: Office multifunction scanners write model-specific Producer strings. Each is individually safe but the set is open-ended and vendor-specific; matching them well needs a real corpus. High value if Joseph's corpus contains scanned paperwork, because these files otherwise get `authored_by = Canon iR-ADV C5535`.
uncertain.design_cite: §2.2 "generated by a tool rather than a person"

uncertain.match: camera firmware strings in EXIF Software
uncertain.rationale: Non-dotted firmware forms (`Ver.1.10`, `1.0.0 (Android)`, `V2.30`) that `tps-bare-version` does not catch. Enumerating them per model is exactly the "thousands of obscure phone models" the brief rules out; a shape-based regex is possible but needs FP analysis against real data first.

sourcing_note: **How to read the `verification` column, because it is not decoration.** Only five pages were opened and read directly while authoring these catalogues; three more were opened by the catalogues-finish agent, who supplied verbatim quotes. Everything else is marked `search_summary`: the fact came from a web-search result summary and the page itself was not retrieved. Those rows say `consulted` rather than `retrieved`, because claiming a retrieval date for a page nobody opened is exactly the kind of unearned confidence these catalogues exist to keep out of the product. A `search_summary` source is not worthless — it is how most of the vendor-prefix and manifest-name knowledge here was gathered — but it must not be quoted as if read, and a row that would be harmful if wrong should be upgraded before launch.
